items.claim: Face modulus alone reaches SF 1 only at Vc 2, where CR-1457's gamma steps from 0.20 to 1; the point is a knife edge that re-optimisation cannot hold (the crimp-branch answers re-check at 0.756/0.789).
items.needed_to_ground: MAINLINE-029's measured crimp-branch gamma at the lead geometry.

items.claim: Explicit 028 joining replaces the 5% joint allowance, as 028 did. Under the 5% floor of 019, 021b and 027, sheet size and bond film stop being levers at all. The reserve is 019's optimistic (sealed-service) set, scaled with radius by 027's laws.
items.needed_to_ground: A ruling on whether the 5% allowance is a floor once joining is explicit.

items.claim: nu 0.08 is the S-200F VHP mean (IAEA) transferred to SR-200 sheet; the inherited 0.33 reads 2.0 percent higher (0.5387 / 0.5818 against 0.5284 / 0.5711).
items.needed_to_ground: A measured in-plane Poisson ratio for cross-rolled SR-200 sheet.

items.claim: The brief's translation of gamma into core shear stiffness per density cannot reach SF 1 (Kc caps at 1). As shape precision, MAINLINE-015's monocoque-equivalent map (t_eq = sqrt(3) h) gives a 2.47 mm dimple at R 10 and 13.1 mm at R 20; that map is a cylinder/monocoque fit applied to a sandwich sphere.
items.needed_to_ground: An imperfection-controlled sandwich-sphere or dome buckling test series.

items.claim: Q is translated to waviness with CR-1457 eq 2.2-12/13 using Fc = 60 psi (typical stabilised compression, taken as the lowest flatwise strength). The lever holds K_delta; physical waviness depends on Ec and Fc (0.347 mm today's equivalent at R 10; 0.099 mm in the Be-kept material combination).
items.needed_to_ground: Measured flatwise tension and bond strength for the Be/CR-III bond, and measured face waviness.

items.claim: Every P3 route to SF 1 needs a qualified SiC design compressive strength of 0.83-1.20 GPa (projection row 0.91 GPa). No design compressive allowable exists; flexure is 380 MPa and 3900 MPa is an unqualified typical value.
items.needed_to_ground: Full-size curved tube compression tests with a Weibull (or other probabilistic) basis.

items.claim: Tube specific stiffness x1.41 (186 MPa per kg/m3) is beyond SiC (best CVD 145). A carbon-fibre tube would need a sourced compressive strength near 0.8-1.2 GPa with that stiffness.
items.needed_to_ground: Sourced UHM carbon tube compressive strength and modulus.

items.claim: A lighter face at beryllium's E and strength (x1.73-1.87, 272-293 MPa per kg/m3) has no thin isotropic candidate: quasi-isotropic carbon is about 100 (a worker estimate with assumed matrix constants); nano-carbon films are lab only.
items.needed_to_ground: Sourced in-plane-isotropic properties of nano-carbon or other candidate face sheets.

items.claim: With beryllium and handbook values kept, the core needs through-thickness stiffness per density of 41-57 MPa per kg/m3, beyond aluminium's 24.8; no carbon-honeycomb compressive modulus was sourced, and the Ultracor shear value is secondary (a 2023 paper quoting 2012).
items.needed_to_ground: A primary carbon-honeycomb datasheet with stabilised compressive modulus.

items.claim: P3 uses 022c's equilateral rows only; the two-way grid is not scored. The finer film grid and polish lift 022c's rows by 1.1 and 1.7 percent (0.7017 to 0.7097; 1.4170 to 1.4412).
items.needed_to_ground: 022's owner's view on the two-way grid's stability with the film.

items.claim: 024's half-of-tensile design rule is carried to every film in the trend (Upilex-S comparison); barrier, creep and seaming are not scored. The 1975 Kapton H row prints no density; Kapton HN's 1420 is used.
items.needed_to_ground: Film design allowables with barrier and creep for Upilex-S class films.

items.claim: Eras not found: beryllium datasheets of about 2006 and 2016; Hexoloy datasheets of about 1996 and 2016; any carbon-honeycomb history; Wright 1965 and JGJ 7-2010 (the lattice 0.4 and 0.2) were not read; Krenzke 1963 not opened. Identical Hexcel tables may mean no re-testing rather than no progress.
items.needed_to_ground: The missing datasheets (Wayback rate limits blocked some).

items.claim: Directions are computed on the lead's CR-III 5056 3/8-1.0; 5056 1/4-1.6 is 2.7 percent better today (0.5425 / 0.5939).
items.needed_to_ground: None for the ranking; factors on 1/4-1.6 would be slightly smaller.

items.claim: The scarf is steepened beyond 30:1 to meet 028's 10 MPa average-shear screen, which is owner-selected, not an allowable; bond and seam strengths are unmeasured (028's rows).
items.needed_to_ground: 028's evidence needs: a weighed, load-tested curved Be/Al panel.

items.claim: The product of factors depends on how a property is parametrised (Q against Ec = Q^2; K_delta against physical waviness). Each lever's definition is stated so a reader can re-weight.
